name: ntfy
description: Simple HTTP-based pub-sub notification service. Send push notifications to your phone or desktop via scripts.
summary: ntfy has been actively releasing updates through mid-2026, with the latest being v2.28.0 (2026-08-27, https://github.com/binwiederhier/ntfy/releases/tag/v2.28.0), a hardening release that caps cache replay sizes at 10 MB per topic, enforces new title (1 KB) and tags (512 bytes) size limits, and extends the visitor bandwidth budget to cover poll-based message replays. v2.27.0 added email-based login and hardened message templating, while v2.25.0 introduced password reset via magic link and upgraded token generation to use a cryptographically secure RNG. Recent releases also promoted PostgreSQL support out of experimental status and added a fail2ban-compatible abuse ban-feed for self-hosted operators.

answers.What is the current license?: Apache 2.0 (based on public repository; not explicitly stated in changelog)
answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes — multiple releases in 2026, most recently v2.28.0 on 2026-08-27
answers.Does it support authentication and acces: Yes — username/password login, email-based login, access tokens, password reset, and visitor bandwidth limits
answers.Is there a hosted cloud version availabl: Yes — ntfy.sh is the hosted cloud version

breaking_excerpts: Message title limited to 1 KB and all tags combined to 512 bytes; requests exceeding these limits are rejected with HTTP 400 (error codes 40057/40058) — previously no size limit existed.

visitor-attachment-daily-bandwidth-limit now also covers messages replayed from the cache by poll requests; heavy pollers consume the same budget as attachment downloads, so operators may need to raise the limit.
Message cache databases from ntfy older than v1.10.0 (November 2021) can no longer be migrated; upgrade via an older ntfy version first, or delete the cache database.

alternatives.name: Pushover
alternatives.review: Paid SaaS, simple API, iOS/Android apps.

alternatives.name: Gotify
alternatives.review: Self-hosted only, real-time push via WebSocket.

alternatives.name: Apprise
alternatives.review: Apprise is a powerful open-source notification library supporting 80+ services but is a library/CLI tool rather than a standalone pub-sub server with a built-in HTTP API like ntfy.

alternatives.name: Pushbullet
alternatives.review: Pushbullet supports cross-device notifications and file sharing but is a closed-source cloud-only service with a restrictive free tier, contrasting with ntfy's open and self-hostable approach.

alternatives.name: Ntopng / Alertmanager (Prometheus)
alternatives.review: Alertmanager excels at routing and deduplicating alerts in observability stacks but is purpose-built for metrics-based alerting rather than general-purpose pub-sub HTTP notifications like ntfy.
